title: Phase Splintering Scheduler — Latency Smoothing & Tenant Fairness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a 'Phase Splintering' scheduling policy that dynamically fragments prefill/decode phases into micro-phases to smooth tail latency while preserving tenant fairness. The policy coordinates with kernel selection and attention-cost hints to decide when to split, merge, or prioritize micro-phases. Goals: reduce 95th/99th latency for mixed short/long workloads, avoid starvation of low-weight tenants, and keep throughput degradation <5% for standard GPT-like models.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th-token latency reduced by >=15% on mixed synthetic workload compared to baseline scheduler. 2) No tenant experiences starvation (p95 request wait time increase <10% vs baseline). 3) End-to-end throughput for steady-state benchmarks stays within -5% of current runtime-1.23. 4) Policy has opt-in toggle and documented config knobs in Console. 5) Unit + integration tests added; e2e perf job in CI passes.
implementation_notes: - Introduce MicroPhase struct with fields: phase_type, token_range, attention_hint_score, kernel_hint. - Scheduler evaluates micro-phase split when attention_hint_score > threshold OR estimated kernel runtime variance > X. - Use exponential backoff merge to avoid fragmentation explosion. - Integrate with kernel selection proxy: when a micro-phase's kernel_hint prefers a quantized fastpath, we allow larger micro-batches; otherwise keep small slices for low-latency. - Add tenant_weight accounting to ensure proportional allocation; weights come from tenant QoS profile.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Aggressive splitting improves latency tail but increases kernel dispatch overhead and memory pressure. - Too many tiny micro-phases can harm throughput due to kernel launch overheads. - Estimation errors in attention_hint_score may cause suboptimal splits; mitigation: conservative defaults and CI synthetic fuzzing. - Interaction with KV cache: splitting must preserve contiguous KV segments or pay extra copy cost.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for MicroPhase state transitions and merge/backoff logic. 2) Integration test with runtime kernel-proxy that simulates varying kernel latencies. 3) Perf harness: mixed tenant workload (50% short chat, 30% long completions, 20% embeddings) with 1k concurrent QPS. Compare metrics vs baseline. 4) Chaos test: inject transient slow kernel (10x) and ensure graceful fallback. 5) Add regression detection in Optimize e2e perf job.
rollout_plan: - Feature flag behind 'phase_splintering_v1' with runtime-1.24. - Internal dogfood in staging with internal tenants for 2 weeks. - Canary on 5% traffic on hosted API (low-risk customers) with telemetry dashboards. - If errors or >10% throughput degradation, auto-roll back to baseline. - After stable, expose config toggles in Console and allow dedicated tenants to opt-in.
performance_targets: p50: <= baseline p50; p95: >=15% reduction target; p99: measurable improvement target (best-effort); throughput_penalty: <=5%
observability_and_metrics: - Expose new metrics: microphases.created, microphases.merged, microphases.avg_tokens, microphases.kernel_hint_mismatch_rate. - Percents: latency_token_95, latency_token_99 per tenant and aggregated. - Tracking: tenant_wait_time_p95, kernel_dispatch_overhead_ms. - Dashboards: phase-splintering overview, kernel-hint correlation heatmap.
